fixture: ex:selfInverse (self-inverse, flagged), ex:hasPart/ex:partOf (a genuine inverse pair -- exercises `.first()` returning a real value that is NOT equal to prop, so no issue), ex:noInverse (no owl:inverseOf triple at all -- the zero-solution case, `.value()`/`.first()` both None, `None == prop` is False) and ex:otherSelfInverse, a self-inverse property deliberately left OUT of main_properties -- the neighbourhood exclusion happens on the driver's argument, not in the graph, since main_properties is itself an argument, not something the region reads from g.

repair 2026-10-30: `@graph g` + `m{ {prop} owl:inverseOf ?v }.first()` was wrong, now `m{ {prop} owl:inverseOf ?v }(g).first()` without `@graph`. `@graph g` binds the block's `owl:` on the CALLER's graph (record ldpy/027, `graph.bind` with override): a graph that spells the OWL namespace `o:` has it rebound to `owl:`, so `_short(prop, g)` (a qname) changed the reported `subject` and message -- driver call 3 (a self-inverse o:topObjectProperty) gave 'o:topObjectProperty' vs 'owl:topObjectProperty'. The call suffix reads g without touching its bindings; constructions updated (`@graph` dropped, `call suffix (g)` added, and `interpolation {expr}`, employed by `{prop}` but never declared).

repair.driver: six calls added after fixture.ttl, graphs built per side: several owl:inverseOf values added in a stated order (first value the property itself -> flagged, first value another -> not flagged although the property is among its values; an incoming owl:inverseOf added first, against a reversed pattern); neighbours sharing two terms (rdfs:subPropertyOf and owl:equivalentProperty to itself, the literal spelling of its own IRI, a blank-node inverse); a self-inverse property in the OWL namespace from a file that binds it as `o:` (the `_short`/`_label` qname reads the graph's bindings); a property with no triple at all; an empty main_properties; the empty graph.
